In modern philological studies, K. R. Norman examines the introductory narrative (*vatthu*) in the commentary to this poem in a discussion of the terms *sañchanna-* and *sañchinna-*, citing the story's description of cultivating mango trees (*ambarukkhā*) before they yield fruit [Norman 1997-2001].

 However, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates substantial Pali-internal repetition, identifying 152 shared segments across 17 texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest reuse partner is the commentary (*Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*), which quotes the verses extensively (67 matches across segments 0.4–8.3) [DharmaNexus]. The text also shares standard stock formulas with numerous other poems in the collection, most prominently the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), the *Bhikkhādāyakavimānavatthu* (Vv 70), and the *Paṭhamaupassayadāyakavimānavatthu* (Vv 68) [DharmaNexus].
